question: What values does the type field in ServiceSpec accept, and how does an Ingress differ from a Service in handling external HTTP traffic?

ground_truth.answer: The type field in ServiceSpec controls how a Service is exposed. ClusterIP (the default) makes the Service reachable only within the cluster. NodePort additionally opens a static port on every Node. LoadBalancer provisions a cloud load balancer and assigns an external IP (available in cloud environments). ExternalName maps the Service to an external DNS name. An Ingress, defined in IngressSpec, is a separate resource type that manages HTTP and HTTPS routing at layer 7, multiplexing multiple Services under a single IP or hostname using IngressRule entries. Unlike a Service of type LoadBalancer (one external IP per Service), a single Ingress can route to many Services based on hostname or path.
context: io.k8s.api.core.v1.ServiceSpec: type field accepts ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, or ExternalName to control Service exposure
io.k8s.api.networking.v1.IngressSpec: defines HTTP/HTTPS routing rules; multiplexes many Services under one entrypoint via IngressRule entries
io.k8s.api.networking.v1.IngressRule: routes requests by hostname and HTTP path to a specific Service backend
